extraction.name: MathVista
extraction.description: MathVista is a benchmark designed to evaluate mathematical reasoning of foundation models in visual contexts. It consists of 6,141 examples derived from 28 existing multimodal datasets involving mathematics and 3 newly created datasets (IQTest, FunctionQA, and PaperQA). The benchmark covers seven mathematical reasoning types (algebraic, arithmetic, geometry, logical, numeric common sense, scientific, and statistical reasoning) and five primary tasks (figure question answering, geometry problem solving, math word problem, textbook question answering, and visual question answering) across diverse visual contexts.
extraction.creator: Pan Lu, Hritik Bansal, Tony Xia, Jiacheng Liu, Chunyuan Li, Hannaneh Hajishirzi, Hao Cheng, Kai-Wei Chang, Michel Galley, Jianfeng Gao
extraction.publisher: UCLA, University of Washington, Microsoft Research
extraction.citeAs: Lu, P., Bansal, H., Xia, T., Liu, J., Li, C., Hajishirzi, H., Cheng, H., Chang, K.-W., Galley, M., & Gao, J. (2024). MathVista: Evaluating Mathematical Reasoning of Foundation Models in Visual Contexts. Published as a conference paper at ICLR 2024. arXiv:2310.02255v3.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: MathVista was constructed by collecting examples from 28 existing multimodal datasets (9 math-targeted QA datasets and 19 VQA datasets) and creating 3 new datasets (IQTest, FunctionQA, PaperQA). For existing VQA datasets, heuristic rules were used to automatically select examples likely to involve mathematical reasoning, followed by manual expert annotation. Each source dataset was limited to up to 400 examples to ensure balanced representation. The three new datasets were manually annotated by graduate students in STEM fields and refined through a rigorous review process.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Manual Human Curator, Web Scraping
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Only 85.6% of examples (5,261 out of 6,141) have annotations. The remaining 14.4% lack annotations due to the heterogeneity of source datasets. Annotations from original data providers lack a unified format and structure.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Data was sourced from 28 existing multimodal datasets including math-targeted datasets (Geometry3K, GeoQA+, GEOS, UniGeo, CLEVR-Math, IconQA, TabMWP, SciBench, TheoremQA) and general VQA datasets (ChartQA, FigureQA, DVQA, MapQA, PlotQA, DocVQA, AI2D, ScienceQA, TQA, A-OKVQA, KVQA, ParsVQA-Caps, TextVQA, VizWiz, VQA2.0, PMC-VQA, VQA-RAD, Super-CLEVR, VQA-AS). Three new datasets were created: IQTest (sourced from puzzle test figures on online learning platforms), FunctionQA (functional plots), and PaperQA (academic paper figures from papers released in August 2023 on Huggingface).
extraction.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: PaperQA sourced from papers released in August 2023 on Huggingface. Multimodal Bard evaluation dates: September 8–10, 2023. GPT-4V evaluation dates: October 7–15, 2023.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: For VQA datasets, heuristic rules were initially designed to automatically select examples likely to involve mathematical reasoning: examples with numeric answers or those containing quantity words in the questions were selected. This automatic filtration yielded 4,949 VQA-format examples. Each source dataset was limited to up to 400 examples. For the testmini subset, a sampling strategy was adopted: (1) randomly sample questions with a threshold number of 4 for each source dataset; (2) randomly sample the remaining questions for each source dataset based on its proportion in the entire set.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Automatic filtration of VQA datasets using heuristic rules (numeric answers or quantity words). Expert annotators manually labeled filtered examples to determine if they involve mathematical reasoning. Majority voting was used to finalize labels. Coarse labels of mathematical reasoning were automatically obtained from source dataset details, with expert annotators manually verifying 1,000 examples. The dataset was divided into testmini (1,000 examples) and test (5,141 examples) subsets. Answer labels for the test set are not publicly released to prevent data contamination.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: For the three new datasets (IQTest, FunctionQA, PaperQA), all questions were manually annotated by graduate students in STEM fields and refined through a rigorous review process. A two-step process was employed: each dataset was independently annotated by three reviewers, achieving a 99.2% inter-annotation consistency rate. Discrepancies (6 out of 736 questions) were resolved through discussion among the entire review team. For VQA dataset labeling, three expert annotators manually labeled examples to determine if they involve mathematical reasoning, with a Fleiss Kappa score of 0.775. For mathematical reasoning category labeling, expert annotators manually labeled 1,000 examples from seven candidates, achieving 94.1% exact match with automatic annotations.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: Custom annotation tool (GUI shown in paper figures). Amazon Mechanical Turk (AMT) for human performance baseline and Multimodal Bard assessment task.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Inter-annotation consistency rate of 99.2% for the three new datasets (only 6 out of 736 questions had disagreements). Fleiss Kappa score of 0.775 for mathematical problem identification among three annotators. For mathematical reasoning category annotation, 94.1% of examples from automatic and human annotations had the exact same set of reasoning types, and 98.79% of individual labels were identical. KL Divergence of 0.008 and Total Variation distance of 0.035 between testmini and the entire set.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The answer labels for the test set will not be publicly released to prevent data contamination; an online evaluation platform will be maintained. The benchmark is part of an ongoing research process with commitment to maintaining datasets (refining potential data noise in response to community feedback) and evolving the leaderboard in response to new models.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: MathVista aims to facilitate the development of AI agents capable of tackling mathematically intensive and visually rich real-world tasks, with applications in educational disciplines, logical queries about statistical data, theorem proving, and scientific discovery. The benchmark highlights significant gaps between current AI models and human performance, underscoring the need for improvements in mathematical reasoning with visual understanding.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset's focus on mathematical reasoning within visual contexts spanning specific domains like science and college-level math may limit generalizability. Annotations were sourced from original data providers, resulting in only 85.6% of examples having annotations with heterogeneous formats. The dataset may have gaps in representation of certain types of mathematical problems and visuals. 30.9% of problems are high-school level and 10.8% are college-level, which influenced the human annotator eligibility criteria.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: While MathVista encompasses a broad spectrum of tasks and visual contexts, there may be gaps in the representation of certain types of mathematical problems and visuals. The scalability and generalizability of the benchmark to other domains remain a concern. Annotations lack a unified format and structure due to heterogeneous sources. The study focused exclusively on the most recent and prominent models given the rapid development in foundation models. Non-English questions (6.57%) require multilingual model capabilities.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Testing and evaluation of mathematical reasoning capabilities of foundation models (LLMs and LMMs) in visual contexts. The testmini subset (1,000 examples) is intended for model development validation or for those with limited computing resources. The test set (5,141 examples) is for standard evaluation. The benchmark supports fine-grained evaluation across mathematical reasoning types, visual context types, task categories, and grade levels.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: 5 human annotators per question for the human performance baseline on testmini. 3 expert annotators for mathematical problem identification and new dataset annotation.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Human performance baseline annotators: required a high school diploma or higher, history of completing more than 5,000 HIT tasks, acceptance score higher than 0.99 on Amazon Mechanical Turk. New dataset annotators: graduate students in STEM fields. Expert annotators for mathematical problem identification: 3 expert annotators.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: GPT-4 (used as answer extractor with >99.5% accuracy on 200 examples). EasyOCR (JaidedAI, 2020) for OCR text detection. Multimodal Bard for image caption generation.
